t2ogxay.name: US-Iran war and Hormuz
t2ogxay.latestHeadline: ‘No war, no peace’: Can Iran break the deadlock with the US?
t2ogxay.summary: At the end of October, Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei warned the US and Israel against returning to war, after threats of a possible resumption of strikes. In early November, Iran said it had agreed to a two-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, shortening an earlier seven-day proposal, while talks with mediators continued in Qatar. On 3 November, explosions were reported on Qeshm Island as US media said the US had carried out strikes, and on 4 November Tehran said four oil tankers had caught fire after hitting mines in the strait. On 6 November, Tehran said ships from India, China, Qatar and Iraq could cross Hormuz freely, and by 8 November the US had launched a task force to disrupt Iran's land-based supply routes. By 10 November Trump said the war would end 'fairly soon', and by 12 November Al Jazeera was describing a 'no war, no peace' deadlock.
